proposals.before: In the Yongping era, Emperor Ming, recalling Fan Ye’s administrative ability in Tianshui, thought no later man had matched him and issued an edict a gift of a million cash to his family.
proposals.after: In the Yongping era, Emperor Ming, recalling Fan Ye’s administrative ability in Tianshui, thought no later man had matched him and issued an edict granting a gift of a million cash to his family.
proposals.reason: The original literal translation is ungrammatical; 詔賜家錢百萬 means an edict granted one million cash to Fan Ye’s family.

proposals.before: He was later found guilty of misreporting land surveys used for taxation, but on account of Li Zhang’s past service the court merely handed him over to the Minister of Justice for judgment instead of harsher punishment.
proposals.after: Li Zhang was later found guilty of misreporting land surveys used for taxation, but on account of his past service the court merely handed him over to the Minister of Justice for judgment instead of harsher punishment.
proposals.reason: The carried subject of 坐度人田不實徵 is Li Zhang; naming him removes the erroneous implication that Chu Xing was charged.

proposals.before: Yet Dou Du and his kin, knowing Zhou Xu’s rectitude and their own long-standing debt to him, never dared touch him.
proposals.after: Yet Dou Du and his kin, despite their long-standing resentment toward Zhou Xu, recognized his rectitude and never dared harm him.
proposals.reason: 怨隙有素 means that their resentment was long-standing, not that they owed Zhou Xu a debt.

proposals.before: Wang Fu was on leave at his villa; Yang Qiu thanked the emperor at court, then filed charges to seize Wang Fu, the attendants Chunyu Deng, Yuan She, Feng (his given name is damaged in the manuscripts), Liu Yi, Pang Training, Zhu Yu, Qi Sheng, and every kinsman serving as a local magistrate—men whose crimes called for wiping out whole clans.
proposals.after: Wang Fu was on leave at his villa; Yang Qiu thanked the emperor at court, then filed charges to seize Wang Fu, the attendants Chunyu Deng, Yuan She, Feng (his given name is damaged in the manuscripts), Liu Yi, Pang Xun, Zhu Yu, Qi Sheng, and every kinsman serving as a local magistrate—men whose crimes called for wiping out whole clans.
proposals.reason: The personal name 庞训 is Pang Xun; “Pang Training” mistakenly translates the given name as a common noun.

proposals.before: Yang Qiu was thrown into the Luoyang jail, executed, and his family driven to the border.
proposals.after: Yang Qiu was thrown into the Luoyang jail, executed, and his wife and children driven to the border.
proposals.reason: Chinese 妻、子 specifies wife and children; idiomatic “his family” erases that kinship detail.

proposals.before: So Yan Gongyan sneered at Huang Ba’s soft ways, and Mi county mocked Zhuo Mao’s kindness—yet even the harshest rule could not win the day.
proposals.after: So Lord Yan sneered at Huang Ba’s soft ways, and Mi county mocked Zhuo Mao’s kindness—yet even the harshest rule could not win the day.
proposals.reason: Chinese 严君 is the honorific “Lord Yan,” not a personal name Yan Gongyan.

decisions.reason: 詔賜家錢百萬 requires a verb of granting; “issued an edict a gift” is ungrammatical, and “edict granting a gift of a million cash” matches the Chinese.
以章有功 marks Li Zhang as the defendant whose merit mitigated the sentence; the prior 兴 subject makes bare “He” wrongly imply Chu Xing was charged.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 后坐度人田不实征，以章有功，但司冠论。

decisions.reason: 怨隙有素 is long-standing resentment, not a debt; the proposed wording restores that enmity while keeping 以䊸公正 as the reason they dared not harm him.
庞训 is the personal name Pang Xun; rendering 训 as “Training” invents a common noun and misnames the attendant.
妻、子徙边 names wife and children specifically; “his family” drops that kinship detail, and the proposal restores it accurately.
严君 is the honorific Lord Yan, not a personal name Yan Gongyan; the proposed replacement matches the Chinese title.
